Meet Ledger

Our technology

It's called Ledger, and I built it for this island.

Instead of renting someone else's software and bending my work around it, I built something that fits how renting really works on Vashon: homes and storefronts looked after side by side, state and county rules to follow, and messages that come straight to me.

What it does for tenants What it does for owners

Built around how renting works here

Three things I wanted Ledger to get right, because they're true of renting on Vashon.

  • Homes and storefronts, side by side

    I look after both, so Ledger does too. A cottage's monthly rent and a storefront's share of its building's shared costs live in the same system.

  • The local rules, built in

    Vashon is unincorporated King County, so Washington and the county both have rules about rent. For homes, Ledger checks late fees and rent increases against them, and stops me if I'd get one wrong.

  • A person in the loop

    Every rental application is read and decided by a person, never turned down by a program. A refund, including a returned security deposit, waits for my approval before any money moves.

For tenants

Your portal is one place for rent, repairs, messages and your lease. It shows you your own account and no one else's.

Paying rent

Rent, paid through Stripe.

Open your portal and you'll see one number: what you owe. Choose bank transfer or card, and you finish on Stripe's own secure page. Your card or bank details go to Stripe, not to me, and Ledger never sees or stores your full card or bank account number.

Every payment gets a receipt in your messages. Bank transfers take a few business days to clear, and Ledger lets you know when yours has been received.

  • Autopay, if you'd like it

    Link a bank account once on Stripe's page, pick any day from the 1st to the 28th, and what you owe is paid for you. You get a reminder three days before each payment, and you can switch it off whenever you like.

  • Tell me what's wrong

    Report a problem, add up to three photos, and mark it urgent if it's water, heat or safety. You can follow your request from received to done, and you're told as it moves.

  • Message me directly

    Write to me from your portal. It's one running thread, kept with your account, and it comes straight to me.

  • Your lease, signed online

    Leases are written from a template and signed on screen. Once everyone has signed, the finished copy waits in your Documents, and your account lists every charge with its due date and whether it's paid.

For property owners

For owners

You get your own login. It shows your own buildings and nobody else's, and the figures come from the same records I work from.

  • A statement every month

    After each month closes, I look over your statement and send it. It shows what came in, what went out, and what's left for you, line by line, and you can download it as a spreadsheet.

  • Your numbers, any time

    Your dashboard shows your latest net income, income and expenses, and how full your buildings are. A short list flags anything worth a look, like an overdue lease or shared building costs running over budget.

  • Ask in plain words

    Type a question about your own portfolio, like how full your buildings are or what your latest statement netted, and get an answer from your real numbers.

  • What happened, in plain language

    An activity page lists payments, statements and repairs on your buildings in everyday words. Pick the dates you want and download it.

  • Shared costs, budget and actual

    If your building has shared costs, you can see the budget next to what has actually been spent, by category.

  • Paid to your own account

    Online rent payments run through Stripe and are paid to your own Stripe account, set up in your name from your owner login.

Kept private

Rent and leases are personal. Here's how Ledger looks after your information, in plain words.

  • You see your own

    An owner's login reaches only that owner's buildings, and a tenant's login reaches only that tenant's own account. The database itself refuses to hand over anyone else's, so it isn't just hidden on screen.

  • Card and bank numbers stay with Stripe

    Payment details are typed into Stripe's pages, not mine. Ledger keeps only the references Stripe gives back, never your full card or bank account number.

  • Passwords are scrambled

    Passwords are stored in scrambled form, so I can't read yours, and everything travels over an encrypted connection.

  • A record that shows tampering

    Important actions, whether mine, a tenant's or the system's, are written to a log that is built so any later change to its history shows up.

Where this website comes in

When a place is ready to rent, I publish it in Ledger. Ledger keeps a public list of what's open, with the address, rent, size and the date it's available, and never a tenant's or an owner's name. That list is made for this website to read.

When a place is rented, I mark it rented in Ledger, and it comes off the list.
